The APO-100-UC is the entry level solution in the Apollo series of unified communication products. The APO-100 is designed for small meeting rooms and huddle spaces. Simply connect the included USB cable to any laptop and instantly have access to a premium conference speakerphone, no drivers or software required. The APO-100 also allows video passthrough via USB. The supplied USB-C cable can be used natively with USB-C equipped devices, or with a standard USB-A 3.0 port using Display Link technology. Use the capacitive touch buttons on the top of the speakerphone to control volume, mute the microphone and even mute the video from your laptop, tablet, or smart phone.
Display Link technology allows the USB-C connection to support both native USB-C source devices and standard USB-A connections from laptops for video transmission and data.

Intuitive capacitive touch buttons provide volume control, mic mute, and video mute for your meeting. An LED ring on the top of the speakerphone provides real-time feedback of volume level and mute status.

recommendedWhen: Camera, microphone, speakerphone, USB peripheral or conferencing workflows are part of the requirement.

salesLanguage.headline: APO-100-UC: improves the meeting experience for people in and outside the room
salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when the room needs to support video meetings, shared audio, cameras, microphones or BYOM/BYOD collaboration.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It helps make the meeting feel joined-up: people can be seen, heard and shared with more reliably than using loose laptop accessories.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Huddle rooms, boardrooms, classrooms and hybrid meeting spaces.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Ask what the remote participant needs to see and hear, then position the product around that experience.
talkTrack: It is about the meeting workflow, not only the hardware.
It helps remove friction around camera, microphone, speaker and USB connectivity.
It should be selected when conferencing is part of the use case.
discoveryPrompts: Which meeting platform is being used?

positioningNotes: Use for UC-led rooms where audio, camera or USB device behaviour matters.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not lead with UC products for simple video switching if there is no conferencing requirement.

systemIntegrator.label: SI / installer
systemIntegrator.headline: APO-100-UC: deployment and commissioning view
systemIntegrator.pitch: Use this view when the installer needs to validate the camera, microphone, speaker, USB and meeting-platform path before the room is quoted or commissioned.
systemIntegrator.value: Turns the sales conversation into practical install checks: location, cabling, signal direction, dependencies, control and commissioning risk.
talkTrack: Check the practical signal path around USB, Audio, HDMI, USB-C video input before finalising the design.
Confirm what connects locally, what leaves the room, and which accessories or endpoints are required.
Check USB class, power method, control path and firmware notes before treating the product as a like-for-like substitute.
discoveryPrompts: Where will the product physically live: table, wall, display, rack, lectern or network closet?
What cable type, distance and route are available between each endpoint?
Which products, receivers, USB devices, controllers or network switches must be present for this to work?
Which meeting platform is being used?
Do users bring their own laptop, use a room PC, or both?
positioningNotes: Good installer language should make dependencies visible before a quote is issued.
Call out install risk early when the product depends on USB bandwidth, network design, endpoint pairing or control integration.
Use for UC-led rooms where audio, camera or USB device behaviour matters.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not imply it is plug-and-play where cable distance, USB class, endpoint compatibility, network design or control programming still needs validation.
Do not lead with UC products for simple video switching if there is no conferencing requirement.

consultant.label: Consultant / technical
consultant.headline: APO-100-UC: architecture fit and trade-off view
consultant.pitch: Use this view to test whether conferencing is genuinely part of the requirement. If the room does not need camera, microphone, speakerphone or USB collaboration, there may be cleaner product paths.
consultant.value: Helps separate a technically possible product choice from the strongest design choice for the application, budget, risk and future expansion.
talkTrack: Validate the application first, then decide whether this product family is the cleanest architecture.
Compare against simpler or more scalable alternatives where the requirement is fixed, expandable, distance-led or conferencing-led.
Use the specification as evidence after the room workflow and signal architecture are clear.
discoveryPrompts: Is this requirement driven by user experience, source/display routing, distance, USB, collaboration, network distribution, processing or control?
What would make this product the wrong choice even if it technically works?
Is the system expected to grow, change rooms, add endpoints, record, stream or integrate with a wider AV platform?
Which meeting platform is being used?
Do users bring their own laptop, use a room PC, or both?
positioningNotes: Use for architectural judgement, product-family selection and proposal-safe trade-off language.
Be explicit when the product is technically possible but unlikely to be the most natural choice.
Use for UC-led rooms where audio, camera or USB device behaviour matters.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not let a feature match override the real application, architecture or operational requirement.
Do not lead with UC products for simple video switching if there is no conferencing requirement.
